definition: Edge inference is the process of running machine learning or deep learning models on local devices (edge devices) such as smartphones, IoT devices, embedded systems, and edge servers instead of centralized cloud computing infrastructure.
details: A key feature of edge computing is edge inference, which allows for real-time data processing, low latency, and improved privacy by reducing the amount of data sent to remote servers.

explainer.lead: Edge inference means using a trained machine learning model directly on a nearby device, such as a phone or embedded system, rather than sending every input to the cloud. This can make responses faster and keep more data local.

tiers.eli5: It is like solving a puzzle at your kitchen table instead of mailing it to a faraway office and waiting for the answer. Your phone or another nearby gadget does the thinking itself, so you get an answer quickly and share less information.
tiers.practitioner: Deploy the trained model on a smartphone, IoT device, embedded system, or edge server, and feed its inputs directly to that local copy. This setup suits applications that need real-time processing, low latency, or less data sent to remote servers; routinely forwarding every input to the cloud undermines those benefits.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a trained model M and an input x available at an edge device d, edge inference computes y = M(x) on d, or on an edge server, instead of on centralized cloud infrastructure. The approach targets real-time processing, low latency, and improved privacy through reduced remote data transfer.

explainer.example: A smartphone runs a deep learning model on an image using its own local inference capability. The prediction is available without first sending the image to centralized cloud infrastructure, reducing latency and remote data transfer.

usedIn.name: Smartphones
usedIn.detail: Run machine learning models locally so inputs need not be sent to centralized cloud infrastructure.

usedIn.name: IoT devices
usedIn.detail: Process data close to where it is generated for low-latency results.

usedIn.name: Embedded systems
usedIn.detail: Perform model inference within the local device rather than relying on remote servers.

usedIn.name: Edge servers
usedIn.detail: Provide nearby inference capacity outside centralized cloud infrastructure.

explainer.intuition: Move the model's prediction work closer to the data instead of moving the data to a distant computer. The device gets an answer with less waiting and less information leaving its local environment.
howItWorks: Place a machine learning or deep learning model on a local edge device or edge server.
Collect an input on that device, such as data from a smartphone or IoT device.
Run the model locally to produce a prediction or other output.
Use the result for real-time processing while reducing the data sent to remote servers.
explainer.whyItMatters: Edge inference supports responsive applications by avoiding a round trip to centralized cloud computing. Sending less data to remote servers can also improve privacy.
misconceptions: Edge inference is not the same as training a model on the device.
It does not require a smartphone; IoT devices, embedded systems, and edge servers can also run it.
It reduces reliance on centralized cloud inference rather than describing a particular model type.
